text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures spent much of Monday drifting narrowly at lower levels with traders growing nervous about the market's ability to continue posting strong gains. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.23, down 0.21 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts drifted lower as an absence of data left the market bereft of inspiration, and dealers said gilts would remain in the doldrums until Wednesday's auction provided a fresh impetus. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113. down 10/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - The French 10-year bond future settled weaker but off its lows in thin range-bound trade with the market waiting for U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress later this week. The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 132.12 down 0.14. from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to higher levels after Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy's revised 1996 deficit was 127.5 trillion lire and that inflation was currently running at 2.4 percent. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.19 up 0.39 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened lower on Monday, following a lackluster London session, with many participants sidelined until Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's mid-week Congressional testimony. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-19/32, down 11/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.66 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures ended slightly higher on Monday due to dealers' short-covering. Investors were mostly inactive ahead of a 10-year JGB auction scheduled for Tuesday. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.09 up 0.18 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - Argentina launched its long-awaited mark Eurobond on Monday, a 1.5 billion mark seven-year deal.
The deal paid a seven percent coupon and was priced to yield 195 basis points over Bunds, considered pricey by the market.
